newsitem.title: UK: JD Sports tumbles on cautious trading news.
newsitem.headline: JD Sports tumbles on cautious trading news.

text.p: Shares in John David Sports Plc fell to a five-month low on Monday as the sportswear retailer warned that like-for-like sales had dropped since the year-end and said some clothing was not selling well.
The stock was down 31-1/2p at 298-1/2 by 0805 GMT, its lowest since late last December, in thin volume of 36,900 shares.
Rivals JJB sports Plc and Blacks Leisure Plc were also dragged down by the JD Sports statement, down 18-1/2p at 486-1/2 and 20-1/2p at 519 respectively.

Reporting a 43 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 9.62 million stg for the year ended March 31 1997, chairman John Wardle said sales had grown strongly in the past year, with the Olympics and the Euro 96 soccer championship giving an added boost.

He said sales since the year-end were 25 percent up on the year before but this was due to the number of store openings, adding that like-for-like sales were down compared with a very strong period a year before.
"It has also become apparent that a segment of the company's clothing offering is not selling well," Wardle added, "and this has contributed to the like-for-like sales performance."
He said action had been taken to address the issue though this would depress profit margins as the stock was cleared from JD's retail chain.
The company, which joined the market last October, reported a 56 percent rise in turnover to 88.07 million stg and said it would pay a dividend of 3.6p per share.
